1. Before you leave

Passports

Sea Cloud requires a biometric passport (any current US passport book qualifies) that stays valid at least six months after the cruise ends. With a December 6 return, both passports need to be valid through at least June 6, 2027. Sea Cloud has registered your passport numbers with the port authorities, so travel on the exact passports listed on your booking. If either passport has been renewed since you booked, tell me right away so Sea Cloud can update it. DOCUMENT NEEDED

A passport card is not enough for this trip because you are flying internationally. Carry the passport books.

St. Maarten entry form (required)

Sint Maarten requires every arriving visitor to complete a free digital Embarkation/Disembarkation (ED) form at https://entry.sx. The government and tourism bureau say it can be completed up to seven days before arrival, so your window is Thursday, November 19 through the morning of November 26. Each of you needs your own form. You will need your passport, the AA2201 flight details, and Simpson Bay Resort as your address. You will get an approval message; airlines may ask to see it at check-in, so screenshot it. DOCUMENT NEEDED TIMING CRITICAL

Watch for look-alike sites

The official form is free and lives only at https://entry.sx. Paid look-alike sites buy ads that appear above it in search results. Type entry.sx directly into your browser, and if any page asks for payment, close it.

The other islands

Antigua, St. Barths and the British Virgin Islands are cleared through the ship as a group, so there is nothing to file in advance for those stops. US citizens need no visa for any country on this route. Follow the daily program for any instruction about carrying passports ashore, and keep a photo of each passport on your phone. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

Europe's new ETIAS travel authorization does not apply to this trip. St. Barths is French, but it is an overseas territory outside the Schengen area, so ETIAS has no bearing on your Gustavia visit.

Health and insurance

No vaccinations are required. Mosquito-borne illnesses such as dengue circulate in the Caribbean, so pack repellent for evenings ashore. Shanon's Allianz Annual Premier policy is in your documents; save the policy number and the Allianz assistance phone number in both phones before you leave.

2. Departure: Dallas/Fort Worth

You stay the night of Wednesday, November 25 at Grand Hyatt DFW (map), which sits inside Terminal D. Check-in is 3:00pm. From the lobby you go straight down to the Terminal D ticket counters and security checkpoint without a shuttle, which is exactly why this hotel suits a 6:00am departure.

Thursday morning, November 26 (Thanksgiving)

  • Flight: American AA2955, DFW 6:00am to Miami 9:48am.
  • Be at the American counter by about 4:30am to check bags. American's bag cutoff on domestic flights is 45 minutes before departure, and Thanksgiving-week security lines can be long at 5:00am. TIMING CRITICAL
  • Check bags all the way through to St. Maarten (SXM). Since both flights are on one American ticket, you will not see them again until St. Maarten.
  • Check your gate in the American app the night before. American flies from several DFW terminals. If your gate is not in D, ride Skylink, the train inside security, which connects every terminal in a few minutes.

3. In the air: connecting in Miami

Outbound (Nov 26): you land in Miami at 9:48am and leave for St. Maarten at 12:11pm, a 2 hour 15 minute connection. This is domestic to international on the same airline, so there is no customs, no bag collection and no second security line. American uses Concourses D and E at Miami; Concourse D is very long, so use the Skytrain if your gates are far apart. This connection is comfortable. SEAM - HANDOVER

Homebound (Dec 6): this is the tight one, and it is covered in detail in section 11.

4. Arrival: Princess Juliana Airport, St. Maarten

You land at Princess Juliana International Airport (SXM) (map) at 4:24pm. The airport opened a new arrivals hall in late 2024. Immigration for US citizens is usually quick, but several US flights land in the mid-afternoon and the line can stack up. Have your passports and the ED approval ready. After immigration you collect your bags and pass customs, then exit to the taxi stand just outside arrivals. SEAM - HANDOVER

Getting to Simpson Bay Resort: step by step

  • Off the plane: follow the arrival corridors and signs straight to Immigration. Have both passports and your ED form approval ready on your phone.
  • Baggage claim: after Immigration, collect your checked bags at the carousel for American Airlines flight AA2201 from Miami.
  • Customs: walk through Customs with your bags and continue straight ahead into the Arrivals Hall.
  • Out the door: exit the Arrivals Hall to the front of the terminal. The taxi stand and its dispatcher desk are right outside, with the posted zone fares. Car rentals are in a separate building across the street, so you do not need to cross the road.
  • At the dispatcher: tell the dispatcher you are going to Simpson Bay Resort, Marina & Spa on Billy Folly Road and confirm the total fare before your bags go in the trunk. The fixed fare to the Simpson Bay resort area is $15 for two people, with a small charge per bag possible. The dispatcher may ask you to share the taxi with other passengers going the same way. Pay the driver in US dollars at the resort.
  • The ride: under 10 minutes, about 1.5 miles. Ask the driver to drop you at the main lobby entrance for check-in.

Taxi stand at Princess Juliana Airport arrivals (map) · Simpson Bay Resort, Marina & Spa (map) DIY FRIENDLY CURRENCY NOTE

US dollars are used everywhere on the island, so there is no need to get local currency at the airport. The resort has an ATM if you need one.

5. Three nights in St. Maarten

Simpson Bay Resort, Marina & Spa (map) is on Billy Folly Road on Simpson Bay beach, a few minutes from the airport. The suites have kitchens, which is handy for coffee and breakfast on your own schedule, and the Simpson Bay restaurant strip is a short taxi ride away. Texas is only two hours behind, so jet lag is not a factor; the long travel day is what you are recovering from.

Thursday evening, Thanksgiving

Keep it simple. After a 4:00am start, dinner at the resort or nearby in Simpson Bay is the right call. Ask the front desk at check-in whether anything special is being served for Thanksgiving. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

How to spend Friday and Saturday

Your last morning on December 6 already includes Marigot, the Simpson Bay Lagoon and the plane-spotting stop at Maho Beach, so use these two days for the parts of the island that tour does not reach. I suggest one easy day and one outing.

Friday, the easy day: the beach and pool at the resort, and a late-afternoon walk or short taxi to Maho Beach (map) only if you want to see the big jets land at full volume (you will get a brief stop there on Dec 6 too). Dinner in Simpson Bay.

Saturday, the French side: take a taxi to Orient Bay Beach (map) for the morning, then lunch in Grand Case (map), the island's best-known dining village, before heading back. Expect roughly $40 to $50 each way by taxi; agree on the fare first. Prices on the French side are often in euros and card payments may process in euros; see the money section on choosing euros at the card terminal. DIY FRIENDLY CURRENCY NOTE

The honest drawback: island traffic

Traffic through Simpson Bay and Cole Bay can be very heavy, and the Simpson Bay drawbridge stops traffic completely when it opens for boats. The local taxi association has publicly warned that the return trip toward Philipsburg can take more than an hour at peak times. Avoid the late afternoon rush (roughly 4:00 to 7:00pm) for any trip you are timing, and never plan a tight return.

Skip Philipsburg on these two days. You will have time there on embarkation day, when it is right next to the pier.

6. Embarkation day: Sunday, November 29

The ship berths at Port St. Maarten cruise pier (map), 79 Juancho Yrausquin Blvd, Philipsburg. Check-in is in the Home Porting Terminal on the pier, where staff inspect passports and hand luggage. SEAM - HANDOVER

Time

Plan

11:00am

Check out of Simpson Bay Resort (confirm checkout time at the desk; ask them to hold nothing, you take bags with you)

About 11:30am

Taxi to the cruise pier. The published fare from the cruise port to the Simpson Bay area is $18 for one or two people, so expect about that plus bags. Allow 30 to 60 minutes for traffic even though the drive is around 25 minutes when clear.

Drop your large bags at the Home Porting Terminal luggage area. Sea Cloud luggage tags are handed out at the pier; write your names on them. Your cabin number is assigned on board, so leave that blank.

12:30 to 3:30pm

Lunch and a stroll in Philipsburg. Front Street is about a 20-minute walk along the waterfront, or take the water taxi from the pier. The boardwalk along Great Bay beach has plenty of lunch spots.

Boarding window. Have passports and the welcome letter in hand.

Front Street and Wathey Square (map) are the heart of Philipsburg, lined with duty-free shops; the narrow lanes between Front Street and Back Street are quieter. If several large ships are in port, Front Street gets crowded and the boardwalk is the more pleasant walk. WALKABLE FROM PIER

What to keep in your carry-on

Your large bags go to the cabin and usually arrive later in the afternoon or early evening. Keep with you: passports, the welcome letter, medications, phones and chargers, valuables, sunglasses and sunscreen, and a change of clothes for dinner in case your bags arrive after you want to dress.

The first hours aboard

Expect a glass of champagne on arrival, then a short settling-in period. The safety drill is mandatory for every guest, and the time is announced on board. The first evening includes the Captain's welcome cocktail; the daily program in your cabin each night tells you the next day's times. The ship leaves at 7:00pm, about an hour after sunset, so the sail-away is in the dark with Philipsburg's lights behind you.

7. Sea Cloud Spirit: life on board

Sea Cloud Spirit is a three-masted, full-rigged tall ship built in 2021, 452 feet long, with 28 sails set by hand and room for at most 136 guests and a crew of about 85. Sea Cloud's ships are among the very few passenger vessels anywhere that are still sailed by hand, so the sail handling is part of the show.

Your cabin and layout

You booked a guaranteed double, which Sea Cloud assigns from Category E (Superior) upward; you receive the number on board. The four passenger decks, from the bottom: the Cabin Deck (most staterooms, boutique, hospital, spa, sauna and the swim platform), the Veranda Deck (restaurant, reception, balcony suites), the Lido Deck (Lido bar and bistro, lounge with the Steinway, library) and the Sun Deck (loungers, fitness area, bridge). An elevator connects all four.

Dining and drinks

Meals are single seating with open seating and no reservations. Breakfast is a buffet in the restaurant, with a lighter early and late breakfast at the Lido Bar. Lunch is a buffet on deck or in the restaurant, afternoon coffee and tea come with sweets and sandwiches, and dinner is a four-course menu with a vegetarian choice. The casual Bistro on the Lido Deck is the alternative to the restaurant at dinner, weather permitting. Once per cruise the chef serves a five-course gala dinner. Your open bar package covers drinks at the bar and the restaurant except premium brands, and wines are paired with lunch and dinner.

Dress

Days are casual yachting clothes. Evenings are smart casual: no shorts at dinner and no swimwear at lunch. For the Captain's gala dinner, guests dress up: a suit for Jeffrey and a cocktail dress for Shanon. Teak decks can be slippery, so bring shoes with non-slip soles.

Practical details

Topic

What to know

Onboard currency

Euros. Your account runs in euros and is settled at the end by card (Visa, MasterCard, Amex, Diners) or US dollar or euro cash. CURRENCY NOTE

Onboard credit

$500 per cabin, usable for bar charges, laundry and the boutique. Not refundable or transferable.

Gratuities

Already included. No crew tipping is expected.

Wi-Fi

Starlink, with 10 GB included; more can be bought at reception. Coverage can drop in some sailing areas.

Laundry

Charged per item for your category, returned next day. No dry cleaning and no irons in cabins.

Medical

A ship's doctor and clinic on the Cabin Deck, complimentary. Emergency phone in every cabin: dial 911.

Reception

Veranda Deck, staffed 7:00am to 11:00pm, reachable by phone any time

Language

English and German; programs and menus come in both

Smoking

Outside areas of the Lido Deck only, never on the Sun Deck, covered areas or balconies

Getting on and off

Through the gangway, which can be steep depending on the tide; tenders and Zodiacs also load from it

Worth doing on board

Watch the crew set sail by hand and lend a hand on the lines if you like. Up to ten guests can climb the rigging to the first platform, about 46 feet above the deck, after a quick fitness check with the ship's doctor (hang from a bar for 10 seconds, balance on one foot for 20 seconds, climb stairs two at a time). The bridge is open to visitors at set times when conditions allow. Snorkel gear, stand-up paddleboards and a towable tube are included, and swim stops from the marina platform happen when the captain approves.

Theme nights: Pirate Night and White Night

Sea Cloud's own name for this sailing is "A Tall Ship's Dream Destination." It is not a costume cruise, so the pirate flavor comes from the islands themselves (Jost Van Dyke and Norman Island are the true pirate haunts) and from one big evening on board. Guests who have sailed Sea Cloud Spirit in the Caribbean report a Pirate Night once per voyage, ending in the crew's sea shanty sing, a long-standing Sea Cloud tradition. Songbooks are handed out, and the ship has pirate hats, swords and eye patches for guests to borrow, so you don't need a full costume. A few touches of your own make it more fun. The same guests describe a White Night with a special buffet on the Lido Deck, where most people dress in white. The DJ at the Lido Bar often keeps going past midnight, so bring shoes you can dance in. The daily program will confirm which evenings these fall on. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

8. Port by port

A good rule for every stop: the daily program lists the exact last tender or all-aboard time, and it is the one to trust. All of your booked tours are Sea Cloud's own, so the ship waits for them; time on your own is your responsibility.

Tuesday, December 1: St. John's, Antigua

In port 8:00am to 1:30pm. ALL-ABOARD RISK St. John's ships dock in the middle of town at Heritage Quay or the neighboring Nevis Street pier, so you step straight onto the waterfront. Heritage Quay (map) is the duty-free shopping strip at the end of the pier, and Redcliffe Quay (map) next door is the nicer of the two, with restored old warehouses holding small shops and cafés. WALKABLE FROM PIER

Your tour: Nelson's Dockyard, 9:00am, about 4 hours, included. An air-conditioned minibus crosses the island with a photo stop at the old Betty's Hope sugar plantation, then climbs to the lookout at Shirley Heights for the classic view over English Harbour, then a guided walk through Nelson's Dockyard (map), the only surviving Georgian-era naval dockyard and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with time for a cold drink by the harbor. The dockyard is across the island from St. John's, so this is a place that needs a tour. NEEDS A TOUR

The honest part: this is a short call. The tour returns around 1:00pm and the ship sails at 1:30pm, so there is effectively no free time ashore afterward. If you want to browse Redcliffe Quay, do it briefly before 9:00am. Antigua drives on the left; look right first when crossing. The local currency is the Eastern Caribbean dollar, but US dollars are accepted everywhere you will go. CURRENCY NOTE

Wednesday, December 2: Gustavia, St. Barthélemy

In port 8:00am to 10:00pm. TENDER PORT The ship anchors outside the harbor and the ship's boats bring you into the center of Gustavia (map). Harbor rules limit boat speed, so tendering is slow; allow extra time. The whole town is walkable in a couple of hours. WALKABLE FROM PIER

Morning tour: Snorkeling in the St. Barths Marine Reserve, 9:00am, about 3 hours, included. Small chartered boats take you to usually two sites of varying difficulty; you climb in and out by ladder over the side. Sea Cloud asks for good swimming ability and some snorkeling experience. Wear your swimsuit under your clothes; towels are provided. Reef-safe sunscreen and a hat.

Lunch: many shops close for lunch, roughly 1:00 to 3:00pm, and some restaurants stop serving after the lunch hour, so eat soon after you get back from snorkeling.

Free time in the early afternoon: Shell Beach (Anse de Grand Galet) (map) is a 10 to 15-minute walk from the landing, a pretty, calm cove covered in small shells. Water shoes help, and you will see relaxed European beach norms. The walk up to Fort Karl above it gives the best view of the harbor. DIY FRIENDLY

Afternoon: Gourmet tasting in the Rothschild Lounge, 4:00pm, about 2 hours. A 10-minute walk takes you to the only Baron de Rothschild lounge outside mainland France for a tasting of several Rothschild wines and their champagne with cheese and fine bites. Sea Cloud lists this one as a surcharge excursion at €195 per person rather than an included tour. BOOK AHEAD VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

Money here is different: St. Barths uses the euro. Cards are accepted almost everywhere, and prices are high. When a card terminal asks whether to charge in dollars or euros, choose euros (see the money section). Taxis are fixed-rate and expensive, and there is no Uber. CURRENCY NOTE

Thursday, December 3: North Sound, Virgin Gorda, BVI

Morning under sail (wind permitting), arrive about 1:00pm, overnight at anchor. TENDER PORT North Sound is a big, sheltered bay ringed by Virgin Gorda, Mosquito Island and Prickly Pear Island. Tenders land at Gun Creek (map), where the tour vehicles wait. The British Virgin Islands use the US dollar.

Your tour: The Baths, 1:30pm, about 4 hours, included. Open safari trucks drive about 40 minutes across hilly country to The Baths National Park (map), a jumble of enormous granite boulders forming pools, grottos and sea caves on white-sand beaches. The trail through the boulders takes about 30 minutes and up to an hour with photo stops; you climb wooden ladders, duck under overhangs and wade through ankle-deep water. Afterward there is time to swim and a rum punch at the Top of the Baths bar. NEEDS A TOUR

What to wear: flat, grippy shoes or water shoes, swimsuit underneath, and a dry bag or zip bag for your phone and camera. If either of you would rather skip the scramble, there is a flatter overland path straight to Devil's Bay beach, and you can meet the group there. The honest part: The Baths gets very crowded at midday when the big-ship tours from Tortola arrive. Your mid-afternoon visit is the better time; those crowds usually thin out by about 3:00 to 4:00pm. HONEST DRAWBACK

Friday, December 4: Sir Francis Drake Channel and Jost Van Dyke

Leave North Sound 7:00am. This morning is the best sailing of the trip. Be on deck from about 7:00 to 10:00am as the ship runs west down the Sir Francis Drake Channel (map), with the mountains of Tortola on the starboard (right) side and the chain of small islands, Ginger, Cooper, Salt, Peter and finally Norman, to port (left). The exact route depends on the wind.

White Bay, 2:00 to 6:00pm. TENDER PORT There is no dock to speak of; plan on a beach landing by Zodiac and possibly stepping into shallow water, so wear water shoes and keep valuables in a dry bag. White Bay (map) is a gorgeous strip of white sand lined with beach bars, including the Soggy Dollar Bar (map), where the Painkiller was invented. Bring cash; Soggy Dollar is known for not taking cards. CURRENCY NOTE

Great Harbour, 7:00 to 11:00pm. The ship repositions around the headland for the evening. Foxy's Tamarind Bar (map) has been the island's legendary sand-floor bar since 1968 and is the natural nightcap. Check the daily program for tender times and the last boat back. Jost Van Dyke is named after a Dutch settler said to have been a pirate, and with fewer than 300 residents it is the least developed stop on the route.

Saturday, December 5: Norman Island, BVI

In port 8:00am to 5:00pm. TENDER PORT Uninhabited Norman Island (map) is the pirate centerpiece of this trip. It is said to have inspired Robert Louis Stevenson's Treasure Island, and treasure really was recovered from its caves. Sea Cloud plans a beach day with a beach barbecue here. The anchorage, The Bight, has the beachside Pirates Bight restaurant and the Willy T, a floating bar moored in the bay.

The famous snorkeling spot is The Caves at Treasure Point (map), around the corner from The Bight. Ask the cruise director on Friday whether a Zodiac run to the Caves is planned, because it is not on your booked program. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

This is the last full day. Expect the Captain's farewell evening, and it is a good idea to pack that night (see disembarkation).

9. Sea days and scenic sailing

Monday, November 30, a full day under sail. This is the day the ship is truly a sailing ship. Sail setting is usually in the morning; the daily program will tell you when. Be on deck for it, then try the rig climb if you are interested, since spots are limited to ten guests. The open-water passage toward Antigua is where you are most likely to feel the motion, and a tall ship heels with the wind. If either of you is prone to seasickness, bring your preferred remedy, and the ship's doctor can help at no charge.

Sunrise and sunset in early December are around 6:20am and 5:40pm. The Sir Francis Drake Channel on December 4 (7:00 to 10:00am) and the morning sail into North Sound on December 3 are the two other times to be outside.

10. Disembarkation: Sunday, December 6

The ship arrives in Philipsburg at 8:00am and everyone must be off by 9:00am, with no exceptions because the next cruise is being prepared. TIMING CRITICAL

Your transfer: island tour with lunch, departing 9:00am. This is booked through Sea Cloud. The tour loops around Simpson Bay Lagoon with a stop at the border monument marking the 1648 treaty that split the island, free time in Marigot (map) on the French side (climb toward Fort Louis for the view, or stroll the harbor), a photo stop at Maho Beach (map) where landing jets pass just overhead, and lunch at a local restaurant. You reach the airport around 1:30pm. SEAM - HANDOVER

Luggage on the last morning

Ask at reception on Saturday exactly how your checked bags travel on the transfer: whether they go out the night before, ride on the tour bus, or meet you at the airport. Pack a day bag with passports, medications, chargers, a light layer for the plane and anything you need for lunch ashore. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

Do not carry fruit from your cabin basket off the ship. Fresh fruit is not allowed into the US and can cause trouble at customs.

11. The journey home

St. Maarten airport

Your flight to Miami leaves at 5:33pm and you arrive around 1:30pm, so you have time in hand. American's counter may not open for your flight right away; if so, find a seat in the departures area and wait. There is no US customs preclearance at SXM, so you will clear US immigration and customs in Miami.

Miami: the tight connection

You land at 8:01pm and AA1679 to DFW leaves at 9:40pm, a connection of 1 hour 39 minutes. Coming in from an international flight, you must clear immigration, collect your checked bags, clear customs, re-drop the bags at American's connection counter just past customs, go back through TSA security, and then get to your gate. American's published minimum for this is 1 hour 35 minutes, so you are only just above it, and Miami's customs hall is among the busiest in the country on evenings when Caribbean flights arrive.

What makes this work:

  • Use Mobile Passport Control through the MIA Airport Official app. It is free for US citizens, needs no pre-approval, and sends you to a dedicated, much shorter line. Set up both profiles before you leave home, then submit the trip on the plane after landing. If you already have Global Entry, use that instead.
  • Sit as far forward as possible on the SXM to Miami flight and move quickly; this is not the time for a restroom or coffee stop before customs.
  • If the inbound flight is late or the line is long, tell an American agent in the customs hall that you are connecting to DFW. If you do miss the flight, American will rebook you; keep receipts in case your Allianz policy's trip delay coverage applies. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

US customs

Declare purchases on the customs form or in the app. US residents returning from these islands generally have an $800 per person duty-free allowance. Do not bring in fresh fruit, plants or meats.

Arriving home

You land at DFW at 12:10am on Monday, December 7. This is a domestic arrival, so just collect your bags and go.

Across the whole route

Cards and US cash. The guilder is pegged at 1.79 to the dollar and you never need it.

On board

Euro account

Settle by card at the end; $500 credit applies first

The currency trap at card terminals: when a card machine or the ship's final bill offers to charge you "in US dollars," decline and choose the local currency (euros in St. Barths, on the French side and on board). The dollar option uses the merchant's own exchange rate, which is almost always worse than your card's. Pay with a card that has no foreign transaction fee. CURRENCY NOTE

Tipping: crew gratuities on the ship are included. On Sea Cloud's tours ashore, a few dollars per person for a good driver-guide is a kind gesture though not required. In restaurants, check the bill first: many places add a service charge (often 10 to 15 percent), and on the French islands service is normally included, so just round up. Where no service charge appears, 15 percent is normal. Taxi drivers do not expect a large tip; rounding up is fine.

Power and connectivity

Dutch St. Maarten, the BVI and the Grand Hyatt use US plugs at 110 volts. The French side, St. Barths and the ship use 220 volts, and Sea Cloud states the ship is 220 V with a razor socket in each bathroom. Bring two European round-pin plug adapters. Phone, tablet and laptop chargers are almost always rated 100 to 240 volts and need only the adapter; check the label. Leave a US hair dryer at home since the cabin has one. Cabins also have a USB charging port at the dressing table.

Phones: the most important habit is putting phones in airplane mode (or turning off cellular data and roaming) whenever the ship is at sea. Ships can connect to a maritime cell network that bills at very high rates. Use the ship's included Wi-Fi on board, and on port days turn on your carrier's international day plan or a Caribbean eSIM if you need data ashore. Check your carrier's current day-pass price before you go. VERIFY BEFORE TRAVEL

Packing

Early December is warm and breezy: highs in the mid-80s°F, nights in the mid-70s, sea temperatures near 80°F, and brief passing showers. Hurricane season officially ends November 30. Pack light, breathable clothes and plan on getting wet on landings.

A few easy pieces each: a bandana or headscarf, a striped or loose white shirt, a sash, big hoop earrings or costume jewelry. The ship lends hats, swords and eye patches, so leave toy weapons at home; realistic replicas are not allowed in carry-on bags

American's standard checked-bag limit is 50 pounds. Sea Cloud sets no weight limit, but standard cabins have limited storage, so soft-sided bags that fold flat under the bed work best.

Time

Every island on this route, and the ship, runs on Atlantic Standard Time all year, two hours ahead of Texas. Miami is one hour ahead of Texas. The ship's clock matches shore time on this route; the daily program will confirm.
